title: Use Checklists to Protect Judgment
coreMove: Convert a repeated costly omission into a short situation-bound checklist and keep judgment awake beyond it.
sourcePressure: The source says people can know a principle and still skip an obvious step under pressure, routine drift, familiarity, or false confidence. Practical reminders and short, relevant checklist protections keep important checks visible, while judgment still handles context beyond the list.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is productivity advice or process worship. The chapter must show a known step disappearing in live conditions and a short checklist catching it without pretending to think for the person.

sourceAnchors.name: checklist framing
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says checklist framing is a practical defense against recurring misjudgment, especially when the list is short, relevant, and tied to repeated situations.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The useful checklist is not impressive; it is the little card that keeps the missed step visible when speed makes memory unreliable.

counterintuition: A checklist makes you less human
tryThisNow: Write a checklist for your day
examples: pilot preflight cliche unless grounded in omission

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: sterile processing team preparing orthopedic instrument trays
exampleSpecs.audience: Grace, a lead technician who has seen the same torque handle missing twice
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a preventable omission delays surgery after everyone thought the tray was complete
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Grace tapes a three-item tray-close checklist beside the washer door and makes the torque handle the final spoken check before sealing the wrap
exampleSpecs.firstImage: steam fogging the small window of the instrument washer

exampleSpecs.domain: climbing gym opening inspection after a belay-device recall
exampleSpecs.audience: Julien, a gym manager opening at dawn with a line of members outside
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether familiarity with the wall makes a recalled device stay clipped for another class
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Julien refuses to unlock the bouldering area until the recall card is checked against each rental bin, even though the front desk is crowded
exampleSpecs.firstImage: chalk dust on the latch of a still-locked climbing gate

exampleSpecs.domain: local newspaper correction workflow after two misspelled names reach print
exampleSpecs.audience: Frida, a copy chief protecting a Friday obituary page
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether deadline pressure makes the staff skip the phone verification they all agree matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Frida circles the two past name errors, then adds a two-person name-read checkpoint before page export
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two clipped obituaries with red circles around family names

exampleSpecs.domain: wedding caterer managing allergy labels during a rushed venue flip
exampleSpecs.audience: Chidi, a catering captain who trusts his team but knows the dessert station changes fastest
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one unlabeled almond tart reaches the wrong guest during service
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chidi makes the dessert runner touch each tray label and read the allergen aloud before the doors open
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Read me the one with almonds," beside silver trays under heat lamps

exampleSpecs.domain: data center migration where the rollback step keeps being assumed
exampleSpecs.audience: Michael, an infrastructure lead facing a 1:00 a.m. cutover
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a familiar migration skips the rollback verification and traps a payments outage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Michael asks the team to point to the tested rollback command before the cutover clock starts, then delays when nobody can show the current script hash
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 12:47 a.m., Michael sees the rollback line blank on the runbook screen
mustAvoid: startup outage war room from chapter 6

exampleSpecs.domain: daycare pickup authorization after a substitute teacher joins midweek
exampleSpecs.audience: Paula, a center director who has the names memorized but knows substitutes do not
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one familiar parent face overrides the written pickup rule
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Paula moves the pickup-card check to the door clipboard and makes every adult show the card before greeting by name
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You hear stroller wheels outside while the substitute reaches for the classroom door

skillTargets: design a short checklist tied to repeated failure
avoid checklist bloat and compliance theater
keep judgment active after the list is complete

tryThisNowSpec: Find one recurring miss and write a three-item checklist that must be completed at the moment the miss usually happens.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
